 Two prerequisites, both must be complete:

1. **Atlas Path** — must show as "Atlas Eternal" in your primary mission log. If it doesn't say that exact name, you haven't finished it.

2. **They Who Returned** — the full Autophage questline. You can confirm it's done if it no longer appears in your mission log at all, and if The Autophage shows up under Catalogue & Guide > Collected Knowledge. To get that questline in the first place, you need to have completed the entire Artemis storyline (showing as "New Beginnings" in your log) and visited a Harmonic encampment on a dissonant planet and broken the seal — you can verify this by checking if the Aeron Turbojet is available as a jetpack option in the appearance modifier.

Once both are done: just engage your pulse drive in space. The quest triggers automatically — your pulse engine will cut out and a Divergence Fragment Space Encounter will appear. Open your communicator when it hails you, have the conversation, and ending the communication starts the mission.

Since you're playing as a Weaver in the current expedition, worth noting that if your save was converted from the Titan expedition, you may already have the Atlantid Drive, and In Stellar Multitudes apparently does not trigger correctly in that case even with all prerequisites met.

This skill never treats lyrics as text alone. Every word exists inside a melodic and rhythmic container. Every line holds a **positional referent** — it points at something: God, the listener, the self, the moment of conversion. All decisions serve that referent first.

Monitors whether lyric rewrites preserve the original emotional trajectory of the composition. Flags arc breaks before they happen.

1. Is this a transmission moment or an immersion moment?

3. If it serves — is there a cleaner way to achieve equal or greater emotional weight while preserving the referent with equal clarity?
   - If yes → use the cleaner way
   - If no → artistic slur is the correct choice

- The altar call is the climax — everything points there

- Chord progressions more sophisticated, dynamics more controlled
- The emotion is interior rather than expressed
- Tier 1 slur preferred; Tier 2 reserved for bridge and final chorus only
- Vocal delivery: trained, clear diction, controlled vibrato

# GOD ABIDES
### Baptist Revival Tent Arrangement
**Key: A major | Vocal: Low female lead / High male tenor**
**Tradition: Baptist Revival — heat builds, body first, spirit follows, altar call is the climax**

---

## STRUCTURE MAP
- Verse 1 — Testimony (confession, isolation)
- Chorus — The turn (God in control)
- Verse 2 — The invitation (call to the room)
- Bridge — The altar call (surrender)
- Chorus — Reprise (congregation joins full)
- Outro — Release

---

## CHORD CHART

**Key: A major**

| Section | Progression |
|---|---|
| Verse | A — D — A — E |
| Chorus | D — A — E — A |
| Bridge | D — E — A — D — E — A |
| Outro | A — D — A (repeat and fade into congregation) |

**Rhythm:** Slow gospel shuffle, 4/4, ~72 BPM. Kick drum on 1 and 3. Snare crack on 2 and 4. Bass guitar walks the chord roots. Piano comps sparse on the verses, fills open on the chorus. Build begins at Verse 2, breaks fully open at Bridge.

---

## LYRIC SHEET

### VERSE 1
*(Lead vocal — raw, low, confessional. Sparse piano only.)*

All alone here today——
I sit around in a cage
Tryin' to make my way
Through this life of mine——

My soul is torn
And my world is lost
My direction gone——
At the cost of the time
It took to figure it out——

### CHORUS
*(Rhythm section enters. Call line delivered firm — this is transmission.)*

**[CALL]** You think you got it bad, child——
But you don't know what it's about——

**[RESPONSE — congregation]** *Don't know, don't know——*

All my life I've seen real terrors
I mean child, I tell you
It'd tear your soul——

**[CALL]** If you think you like evil——
**[RESPONSE]** *You don't know——*

Ride above me or ride below
With God in the sky——
Now in control————

---

### VERSE 2
*(Vocal opens up — still confessional but now an invitation. Bass and piano fuller.)*

Lead me away
From the darkness in my heart——
Take me true to this——
The Lord above, my home——

All I know here today
I know it's gone——
And I say——

Just hang out if you can, child——
'Cause your life ain't sh—
*(vocal swallows the word — congregation knows, congregation feels it)*
If you got what it takes to begin——

---

### BRIDGE — ALTAR CALL
*(Everything drops to piano alone. Then builds bar by bar. This is the climax.)*

No matter how far——
Or how deep down the road
To hell you leapt or creeped——
You're gonna get away————

All you got to do
Is turn to God and tell him so——

**[CALL — full voice now, rhythm section all in]**
I know I'm wrong——
And I'm ready to go————

Ready to let it all
Drop away from me——

So just reach on down, Lord————
Reach inside————
Find my heart now
And let it ride————

Into the day————
And away from the night————

---

### CHORUS REPRISE
*(Congregation is in. Full sound. Tier 2 slur on "child" every time — let it drag, let it reach.)*

'Cause I'm here to tell you
Even you, child——
No matter how far you have fallen
Or what you do——

You have a place
In the Lord's good plan————

And if you take the time
To reach inside——
Seein' yourself
That you want to abide——

With the man above
As much as you just want to be free————

---

### OUTRO
*(Slow, open. Piano holds. Congregation breathes.)*

So child—— if you've got the stomach
To rise above and let it run——

Then let it go————
And ride with me————

And with the good Lord
Standing beside you——
In yourself and abide you————

You will get
What you need
To see————

Today————————
